result:
My verdict for DG5 round 4 is **BLOCKED**. This run's sandbox won't let PostgreSQL start, so the integration and browser checks, which cover most of the acceptance criteria, could not run.

**The blocker.** All three database harnesses (`with-pg.sh`, `with-stack.sh`, `with-demo-stack.sh`) run PostgreSQL as uid 1000 through `unshare --user`. This run's shell sandbox forbids new user namespaces (`max_user_namespaces` is 0, only uid 0 is mapped), and PostgreSQL refuses to run as root (`03-sandbox-userns-blocker.log`). The earlier R4B run could start PostgreSQL, so the sandbox has changed since then. I did not try to get around it; changing the sandbox is your call.

Because of that, these are BLOCKED:
- both integration runs, `contract.test.ts` and `tests/qa` on its own;
- every product, root and demo e2e run, and the read-only auditor pass;
- the A06/A07/A15/A16 suite counts and the exported samples that REQ-DLV-037 requires;
- the stack re-runs needed to verify F-DG5-144.

Re-running in a session whose sandbox allows that user namespace would unblock all of them.

**What ran and passed** (frozen candidate `sha256:26d4ad92…`, 2188 files, confirmed at start and end):
- **Static checks:** all seven exit 0.
- **Unit tests:** six full runs, all green (Node 22 and 24, both locale settings, plus two Node 22 runs in parallel at load 19.4). The 18 stderr blocks are the same ones seen in rounds 2–3.
- **Validators:** `--register DG5`, `--pipeline`, and the historical DG1–DG4 checks all pass.
- **Repair diff:** no behaviour is weakened, and the orchestrator's `2d0f98c` changes comments only.
- **Offline export samples:** rendered without a database in every format, in English and Arabic. The Arabic files carry right-to-left markers, missing values show Unknown rather than 0, and provisional values are labelled. This exercises the renderers only and does not count towards REQ-DLV-037.

**Open findings I was asked to verify:**
- **F-DG5-145 (Low): closed and verified.** The full module walk took 16–27 s against its new 150 s budget (5.5–9.1× headroom). A real rule-4 mutation is caught by the new guard test. The mutation that survives is an equivalent one, like disclosed observation (o).
- **F-DG5-144 (Medium): left open, not judged a failed fix.** The required re-runs on the demo stack couldn't happen. As a database-free substitute I rendered the real Diagnose screen and the 409 conflict banner and laid them out in Chromium with the built stylesheet, at 390 px, 320 px and 200 % text, in English and Arabic. The page doesn't scroll sideways, every register scrolls inside its own named region, and no Arabic header is broken mid-word. With the repair's CSS reverted, the overflow comes back (356–697 px on Diagnose), so the check isn't vacuous.

**New finding:**
- **F-DG5-146 (Medium, non-mandatory; owner frontend-ux-engineer).** It is the same defect class as F-DG5-144, on two P5 screens:
  - **Form builder field table** (`FormSchemaPage.tsx:234`): its wrapper uses a `.table-scroll` class that no stylesheet defines.
  - **T14 Attachments table** (`FormFramework.tsx:1001`): it has no wrapper at all.
  - **Effect:** the page scrolls sideways at 390 px and 200 % text in both languages, by up to 281 px at 390 px and up to 562 px at 200 % text, with columns cut off.
  - **Limits:** the export dialog (`ExportDialog.tsx:125`) uses the same unstyled wrapper; I didn't lay it out, but it is very likely affected too. The overflows were found on rendered snapshots of the real components, not on the running stack.

  Elsewhere, my layout sweep of 156 snapshots of P5 screens found no serious or critical accessibility issues apart from one artefact of the snapshot method.

**D-175 observations:**
- **(n) accepted** as a readability point. At 200 % text, ordinary English words in the narrow Diagnose statement column break mid-word. This predates the repair, and Arabic words and column headers never break.
- **(o) accepted**, as above.
- **(l) and (m)** need the integration tests, so they are left for the re-run. No test pins the old record counts or checksum.

Across the 78 requirements, every one also names at least one database or browser test, and 25 have no unit test at all. So none can be shown complete in this run.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG5/round-4/`:
- qa-verifier.json
- qa-verifier.findings.json
- qa-verifier.verifications.json
- qa-verifier.md

Evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/round-4/`, and probe sources are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG5/qa/tests/round-4/`.
